problem_text:
A regional water utility must devise a pumping and storage schedule for a critical reservoir over the next 20 weeks.  
The initial water volume in the reservoir at the start of the planning window is 24 megaliters.  
In each week t = 1, …, 20, the utility may authorize a pumping run from a distant aquifer; the amount pumped must be between 6 and 38 megaliters.  
Each pumping run, however, requires a 4‑week pipeline transit period before the water becomes available for distribution or for adding to reservoir stocks.  
Weekly consumer demand for water (in megaliters) is forecasted as:  
Week 1: 36  
Week 2: 25  
Week 3: 11  
Week 4: 41  
Week 5: 28  
Week 6: 19  
Week 7: 43  
Week 8: 50  
Week 9: 33  
Week 10: 57  
Week 11: 53  
Week 12: 19  
Week 13: 17  
Week 14: 42  
Week 15: 30  
Week 16: 30  
Week 17: 53  
Week 18: 56  
Week 19: 14  
Week 20: 33  

Service shortfalls are tolerated, but any weekly demand not met is simply lost and cannot be deferred to a later week.  
Throughout the 20‑week horizon, water volumes may be treated as continuous quantities, and the total volume stored in the reservoir at any moment must not surpass its safe capacity of 38 megaliters.  
The total operational cost comprises three elements: a pumping cost of 6 per megaliter extracted; a storage cost of 2 per megaliter held in the reservoir from one week to the next; and a shortage penalty of 12 per megaliter of unmet weekly demand.  
The utility seeks to determine the optimal pumping quantity for each week and to monitor the resulting reservoir volume and weekly deficit so as to minimize the aggregate cost.
